title: Order cancellation
stakes_rationale: Adds a state transition other flows read and a new event type the warehouse consumes.
summary: Adds a cancel transition to the order service and its endpoint, publishes `order.cancelled` on the existing FIFO queue, then adds the Cancel order button to the web order page.

success_criteria.text: Build passes: `npm run build` in backend and web.
Cancelling ACTIVE order `o-1` as its owner returns 200 and sets CANCELLED.
Cancelling as another user returns 403 and leaves the order ACTIVE.
One `order.cancelled` message with group `o-1` reaches the queue.
The order page shows Cancel order for an ACTIVE order.
The order page hides Cancel order for a SHIPPED order.

phases.name: Cancel transition
phases.test_rationale: Step 1.1 adds a transition with two rejection branches.
phases.context: This is the first phase. No prior phases.

requirements.statement: WHEN the owner of an ACTIVE order requests its cancellation THE SYSTEM SHALL set the order status to CANCELLED.
IF the caller does not own the order THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the cancellation with status 403.
WHEN an order is cancelled THE SYSTEM SHALL publish `order.cancelled` carrying the order identifier.

constraints.fact: `MessageGroupId` is required for every message sent to a FIFO queue.
constraints.rule: Set the order id as the message group of `order.cancelled`.

steps.title: Add the cancel transition
steps.action: Add method `cancel(id: string, userId: string): Promise<Order>`. Logic: (1) load by `id`, throw `NotFound` if absent; (2) throw `Forbidden` when `order.userId` differs from `userId`; (3) throw `InvalidState` unless status is ACTIVE; (4) set CANCELLED and save; (5) publish `order.cancelled` with `orderId`.

binding_rules.rule: Set the order id as the message group of `order.cancelled`.

steps.title: Add the cancel route
steps.action: Add `POST /orders/:id/cancel`, calling `OrderService.cancel` with the session user and mapping `Forbidden` to 403 and `InvalidState` to 409.

phases.name: Cancel button
phases.test_rationale: Step 2.1 adds a status branch that decides whether the button renders.
phases.description: Shows Cancel order on ACTIVE orders and calls the endpoint.
phases.context: Phase 1 added `POST /orders/:id/cancel` in the backend repo: no body, 200 with the order JSON, 403 when the caller does not own the order, 409 when it is not ACTIVE.

requirements.statement: WHILE an order is ACTIVE THE SYSTEM SHALL show a Cancel order button on the order page.

steps.title: Add the button
steps.action: Render a Cancel order button only when `order.status` is ACTIVE. On click, call `POST /orders/:id/cancel` and replace the order with the response.

risks.risk: The warehouse consumer ignores unknown event types.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate the consumer change before release.

verification: **Final:** each repo's `build` command after its phases.
